span.label: the cortical basis of auditory backward masking, and whether its unusually long maturation in children is visible in cortical responses
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: whether standard onset-responsive cortical neurons show backward masking at all, and whether juveniles show more of it than adults
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: backward masking is present in ordinary cortical neurons, arises from both suppressed tone firing and a reduced dynamic range, and is larger in juveniles - mainly through the suppression
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Inhibition evoked by the masker arrives with a shorter latency than excitation, so it can reach back and suppress the response to the tone that preceded it.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: In immature cortex the inhibitory response to the masker is larger and slower to decay, so it truncates more of the preceding excitatory tone response and amplifies firing-rate suppression in juveniles.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Juveniles integrate over a longer listening window, which pulls more masker-driven firing into the comparison baseline, shrinking the dynamic range and raising masked thresholds.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Unrefined inhibition in cortex or in presynaptic regions lets an off-frequency noise masker suppress juvenile responses more than adult ones.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: masking arises from a reduction of the signal response together with a higher comparative baseline, which narrows the dynamic range available for detection
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: and a shorter latency for inhibition than for excitation lets the later masker suppress the earlier tone, which also explains why a suppressed masker response masks less
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: so the cortical effect may be inherited from earlier regions, with cortex possibly adding to it by reducing rebound excitation
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: and the immature version is attributed to inhibition that decays more slowly and summates more in young neurons

span.label: RETRACTED (AN ACCOMPANIMENT READ AS A CAUSE, AND THE AGE RUNS THE WRONG WAY) · maturation —causes→ suppression
span.note: RETRACTED: AN ACCOMPANIMENT READ AS A CAUSE, AND THE AGE RUNS THE WRONG WAY. The edge is `maturation --causes--> suppression`. The span: 'Tone threshold shifts were LARGER IN JUVENILES THAN IN ADULTS, indicating greater cortical backward masking. Quotation withheld.' Two faults. `Accompanied by` is co-occurrence - the paper is reporting that two measures move together, not that one produces the other. And the direction is inverted: SUPPRESSION IS LARGER IN THE LESS MATURE ANIMALS, so if maturation acted on it at all it would reduce it. The paper's title is `Late maturation of backward masking`, and the finding is that the juvenile state has MORE of this, not less. Found by the neighbour query (Q-400). Q-411. — strength of the relation: 1 — larger shifts in juveniles with larger firing suppression, and NO difference in dynamic range reduction - so the two elements dissociate across development

span.label: Most auditory cortex neurons required a louder tone to be detected when a noise masker immediately followed the tone, demonstrating backward masking in ordinary onset-responsive cortical cells.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Cortical backward masking arises from two things at once: the masker suppresses the tone-evoked response, and it raises the baseline so that the dynamic range available for detecting the tone shrinks.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Juvenile units showed significantly larger masked threshold shifts than adult units under both analysis windows.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Tone-evoked firing was suppressed by the masker more strongly in juveniles than in adults under both analysis windows.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The masker-induced reduction of dynamic range was the same size in juveniles and adults, so the age difference in masking was not driven by dynamic range.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Units that gave no response at all to the noise alone still showed significant masked threshold shifts, so a response to the masker is not required for backward masking.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Population threshold shifts computed over the whole trial (~18-43 dB in adults) matched human psychophysical backward-masking shifts far better than shifts computed over the narrow tone window (~13-16 dB).
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: In units that did respond to the noise alone, the preceding tone significantly suppressed the noise-evoked firing, i.e. forward masking occurred alongside backward masking in both age groups.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Pooling all units into a population neurometric also produced larger threshold shifts for juveniles than for adults under both windows.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Within the narrow tone window, the loss of dynamic range predicted the masked threshold shift only in juveniles, suggesting juveniles rely more on dynamic range for detection.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Adding the backward masker delayed the tone-evoked first spike only slightly in both age groups, so latency shifts are not the basis of the masking.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: backward masking has a longer maturational trajectory than many other auditory percepts, and its neural correlates are not well described at any developmental stage
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND THE TWO WINDOWS GIVE DIFFERENT ANSWERS: neural threshold shifts match human psychophysics better when the longer window is used
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THE ANALYSIS WINDOW IS A CHOICE, WITH THE REASONS GIVEN BEFORE THE RESULT: one isolates backward masking uncontaminated by forward masking, the other includes the masker response
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THE LOCUS ARGUED FROM WHERE IT IS AND IS NOT FOUND: present in inferior colliculus, absent in auditory nerve and cochlear nucleus, impossible peripherally because the signal precedes the masker
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: with variability itself taken as INDICATIVE of central contributions, being greater in backward than forward masking
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the area was chosen because inactivating it impairs temporal discrimination and because human imaging ties it to conscious masked detection
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: juvenile neurons showed both greater tone-firing suppression and larger threshold shifts, at single-cell and population levels
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A POOLING DECISION JUSTIFIED BY THE COMPOSITION OF THE SAMPLE: single and multi-units pooled BECAUSE the multi-units dominated
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THE METHOD IS ALIGNED TO THE LITERATURE IT WILL BE COMPARED WITH: monaural delivery, to parallel the majority of psychophysical studies
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND THE INCLUSION RULE IS SET BY THE PERCEPT: only units responding reliably to short tones, because backward masking is reliable only for short tones

span.label: this is the first assessment of backward masking in STANDARD onset-responsive cortical neurons, and both coding elements contribute

span.label: with the two elements dissociating across development - larger suppression in juveniles but no difference in dynamic range reduction

span.label: A CORRELATE THAT IS NOT THE CAUSE, SAID PLAINLY: suppression correlated with masking but could occur in its absence

span.label: a shorter latency for inhibition than excitation lets the later masker suppress the earlier tone, and predicts the negative correlation observed

span.label: so the cortical effect may be inherited from earlier regions, with cortex possibly magnifying it

span.label: children LISTEN LATE with respect to a signal, and may be integrating over a longer window than adults

span.label: and the slow maturation attributed to inhibition, which decays more slowly and summates more in young neurons
